F2-L04.intro: Say where you are from (أَنَا مِنْ …), give a nationality that matches the person (بِرِيطَانِيٌّ / بِرِيطَانِيَّةٌ), and say which languages you speak, understand, read and write — asking back to a boy and to a girl.

tasks.task: Say which country you are from.
ASK the leader where he is from (he then answers).
tasks.en: And you, where are you from?

roleplays.setting: An online class with students abroad
roleplays.title: Meeting Nour from Cairo

tasks.examiner: مَرْحَبًا! أَنَا نُورُ. مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
tasks.task: Say where you are from and where your family is from.
tasks.model: أَنَا مِنْ بِرِيطَانِيَا، وَأُسْرَتِي مِنْ بَاكِسْتَانَ.
tasks.en: I am from Britain, and my family is from Pakistan.

tasks.task: ASK her nationality — to a girl (she then answers).
tasks.en: And you, what is your nationality? (to a girl)

tasks.task: Name two languages you speak and one you are learning.
tasks.en: I speak English and Urdu, and I am learning Arabic.

tasks.task: Say what you can do in Arabic.
tasks.model: نَعَمْ، أَقْرَأُ العَرَبِيَّةَ، وَأَكْتُبُ بِهَا قَلِيلًا.
tasks.en: Yes, I read Arabic and write it a little.

tasks.task: Answer the unexpected question, with a reason.
tasks.model: نَعَمْ، أُمِّي تَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ، لِأَنَّهَا مَغْرِبِيَّةٌ.
tasks.en: Yes, my mother speaks Arabic, because she is Moroccan.

tasks.examiner: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِكَ: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟
tasks.task: Give your nationality and your family’s origin.
tasks.model: أَنَا بِرِيطَانِيٌّ، وَأُسْرَتِي مِنَ اليَمَنِ، لِذٰلِكَ أَنَا عَرَبِيٌّ أَيْضًا.
tasks.en: I am British, and my family is from Yemen, so I am Arab too.

tasks.examiner: مَا اللُّغَاتُ الَّتِي تَتَكَلَّمُهَا فِي البَيْتِ؟
tasks.task: Say which language you use with whom.
tasks.help: فِي البَيْتِ نَتَكَلَّمُ … مَعَ … ، وَ… مَعَ …
tasks.model: فِي البَيْتِ نَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ مَعَ جَدَّتِي، وَالإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ مَعَ إِخْوَتِي.
tasks.en: At home we speak Arabic with my grandmother and English with my siblings.

tasks.task: Describe two classmates, a boy and a girl, with matching nationalities.
tasks.model: نَعَمْ، زَمِيلِي عَلِيٌّ بَاكِسْتَانِيٌّ، وَزَمِيلَتِي سَارَةُ سُورِيَّةٌ.
tasks.en: Yes, my classmate Ali is Pakistani, and my classmate Sara is Syrian.

tasks.examiner: … أَنَا مَغْرِبِيٌّ، وَأَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَالفَرَنْسِيَّةَ وَالأَمَازِيغِيَّةَ.
tasks.task: ASK his nationality and languages in one question (he then answers).
tasks.model: وَأَنْتَ، مَا جِنْسِيَّتُكَ، وَأَيَّ لُغَاتٍ تَتَكَلَّمُ؟
tasks.en: And you, what is your nationality, and which languages do you speak?

tasks.task: Answer the unexpected question with two reasons.
tasks.model: أُحِبُّ العَرَبِيَّةَ أَكْثَرَ، لِأَنَّهَا لُغَةُ القُرْآنِ، وَلِأَنَّنِي أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ بِهَا مَعَ جَدَّتِي.
tasks.en: I like Arabic most, because it is the language of the Qur’an, and because I can speak it with my grandmother.

conversation.en: Yes, I understand Arabic a little.

conversation.q: مَا جِنْسِيَّةُ وَلَدٍ وَبِنْتٍ مِنْ مِصْرَ؟
conversation.qen: What is the nationality of a boy and a girl from Egypt?
conversation.en: The boy is Egyptian (m.), and the girl is Egyptian (f.).

conversation.qen: Which languages do you speak and read?
conversation.model: أَتَكَلَّمُ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ وَالأُرْدِيَّةَ، وَأَقْرَأُ العَرَبِيَّةَ أَيْضًا.
conversation.en: I speak English and Urdu, and I read Arabic too.

conversation.q: كَيْفَ تَسْأَلُ بِنْتًا عَنْ جِنْسِيَّتِهَا وَلُغَتِهَا؟
conversation.qen: How do you ask a girl her nationality and language?
conversation.en: What is your nationality? And which language do you speak? (to a girl)

conversation.qen: Where is your friend from, and what is his language?
conversation.model: صَدِيقِي مِنَ الأُرْدُنِّ؛ هُوَ أُرْدُنِيٌّ، وَيَتَكَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَالإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ.
conversation.en: My friend is from Jordan; he is Jordanian, and he speaks Arabic and English.

conversation.qen: What is the difference between “ʿarabiyyun” and “ʿarabiyyatun”?
conversation.model: «عَرَبِيٌّ» لِلْوَلَدِ أَوِ الرَّجُلِ، وَ«عَرَبِيَّةٌ» لِلْبِنْتِ أَوِ المَرْأَةِ؛ نُضِيفُ «ـةٌ» لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ.
conversation.en: “ʿArabiyyun” is for a boy or man, and “ʿarabiyyatun” for a girl or woman; we add -a for the feminine.

conversation.model: أَتَعَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ لِأَنَّهَا لُغَةُ القُرْآنِ، وَلِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي العَرَبِ.
conversation.en: I am learning Arabic because it is the language of the Qur’an, and because I want to talk with my Arab friends.

conversation.qen: Introduce yourself: country, nationality and languages.
conversation.starter: أَنَا مِنْ … ، وَأَنَا … . أَتَكَلَّمُ … ، وَأَقْرَأُ … وَأَكْتُبُ … أَيْضًا
conversation.model: أَنَا مِنْ بِرِيطَانِيَا، وَأَنَا بِرِيطَانِيٌّ. أَتَكَلَّمُ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ وَالبِنْغَالِيَّةَ، وَأَقْرَأُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَأَكْتُبُ بِهَا أَيْضًا.
conversation.en: I am from Britain and I am British. I speak English and Bengali, and I read and write Arabic too.

conversation.q: أَيَّ لُغَةٍ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتَعَلَّمَ فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ؟
conversation.qen: Which language do you want to learn in the future?
conversation.starter: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ … فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ، لِأَنَّنِي …
conversation.model: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ الفَرَنْسِيَّةَ فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ، لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ السَّفَرَ إِلَى فَرَنْسَا وَالمَغْرِبِ.
conversation.en: I want to learn French in the future, because I love travelling to France and Morocco.
